name: Dermatology & skin (category guide)
summary: National Skin Centre vs private derm cash rates — foreigner fee honesty, aesthetic upsells, and when a GP trial beats a S$300 first consult.
body: Foreigners on EP/DP are not entitled to citizen/PR subsidies at the National Skin Centre — public queue + full foreigner fees can cost more than a transparent private clinic, which is why askSingapore threads warn against assuming ‘government = cheaper’. Private derm first consults commonly land in the low-to-mid hundreds SGD before procedures or isotretinoin labs; ask for the consult fee and typical add-ons in writing. Aesthetic / laser packages are a different product from medical dermatology for acne, eczema, or suspicious moles — decline hard-sell packages until you have a diagnosis. Many corporate outpatient riders exclude dermatology or reimburse only when referred for a medical (not cosmetic) indication — read the schedule. Start with a panel GP for straightforward rashes or mild acne; escalate to a SMC-registered dermatologist for scarring acne, unexplained lesions, or treatments that need blood monitoring. Verify the doctor on the Singapore Medical Council register. This is a category guide, not a ranked clinic list.
whenToEngage: Acne / eczema not responding to GP care
Quoted private derm fees or package hard-sell need a sanity check
NSC foreigner fees vs private cash unclear
Outpatient rider may exclude dermatology / aesthetic codes
